The age: The age runs from {rules.start} to the armistice of {rules.end.season|season} {rules.end.year}.
The {events.greatWar.name} breaks out in the {rules.greatWar.season|season} of {rules.greatWar.year}.
Heirs: Each heir card offers {rules.heirs|word} heirs, and the player may deal again {rules.rerolls|word} times a game.

Every heir is a rarity and a trait. A {rarities.0.name} or {rarities.1.name} ruler has a bonus and a malus; from {rarities.2.name} on he also brings a one-time bonus at his coronation. The rarer he is, the bigger the bonus and the smaller the malus.
More rerolls will be for sale at ${rules.price.reroll} each; they are not for sale yet.
Reigns: A reign lasts {rules.reign.years.0} to {rules.reign.years.1} years if nothing ends it sooner.
Each year a ruler has a {rules.reign.murder|pct} chance of being assassinated.
A ruler beaten in a war he started, or one that cost him land, abdicates {rules.reign.abdicate|pct} of the time.

Besides a {rulers.flirt.label}, whose reign always ends in one, {rules.reign.crisis|pct} of successions end in civil war, which adds {rules.reign.crisisUnrest} unrest everywhere and lasts {rules.reign.crisisYears.0} to {rules.reign.crisisYears.1} years; meanwhile the army fights at {rules.reign.crisisArmy|frac} strength.
In a nation whose unrest is above {rules.reign.coupUnrest}, the army stages a coup in {rules.reign.coup|pct} of seasons and crowns a ruler of its own choosing: no heir card.
A ruler plans at least {rules.horizon.min} years ahead, and up to {rules.horizon.span} more the more patient he is.
Armies: Every soldier is a worker lost: the work done in fields and factories falls with the size of the army, as if {rules.workers}k men per million people would empty them, but it never falls below {rules.workersMin|pct}.
An army that wins a battle with more than {rules.breakthrough|times} the strength of the other side breaks through and advances twice.
Building: A factory takes {rules.build.factory|word} seasons to build, a fortress {rules.build.fort|word} and {rules.price.fort} gold.
Reforms cost {rules.reform.cost} gold and take away {rules.reform.calm} unrest; they can be passed again after {rules.reform.wait|years}.
Unrest and war: A province with unrest of {rules.unrest.restless} or more is restless; at {rules.unrest.uprising} or more it can rise.
Weighing a war, a ruler counts {rules.settle|pct} of the time a conquest takes to become integrated.
New nations: A nation born in an uprising starts with {rules.newNation.gold} gold and an army of {rules.newNation.armyPerMillion}k men per million people. It leans to war and plans ahead as its own entry says.

Its relations with the nation it broke from start at {rules.newNation.hostility}, but the two keep the peace for {rules.newNation.truce|span}. A great power on bad terms with the old ruler may guarantee its independence for {rules.newNation.guarantee|span}.

When an uprising wins in a province next to a living nation of its own people, the province joins that nation. Otherwise the province's own fallen nation comes back if it was of the same people, or else the people rises as its nation that was not on the map in {rules.start}, or else as its only nation. A people with several nations and none of them new, like the Germans, finds no allies.
Alliances: An ally comes to a nation's defence {rules.allies.defend|pct} of the time, and always if it guaranteed that nation's independence. It joins an attack {rules.allies.attack|pct} of the time, and only if the two are on good terms.

A nation can unite with a smaller nation of its own people by treaty once their relations reach {rules.unite.relations} and it is more than {rules.unite.power|times} as powerful, unless the smaller one has another great power for an ally.
